To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
global-scale flood risk modelling can be performed using the model cascade presented in this paper.
we developed a model cascade to produce global flood risk maps based on multiple flood return-periods and validated this cascade.

(1) the developed model cascade is a robust tool to produce global-scale flood risk maps; (2) the cascade is sensitive to the choice of climate forcing data and the assumed flood protection level; (3) the model cascade can be applied to other natural hazards, such as drought, and can be adapted to other impact indicators, such as the number of flooded buildings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
assessing global-scale flood risk.
developing a global flood risk model that can be used in a wide range of applications.
developing a model cascade to assess flood risk at the continental and global scale.

we have developed a global flood impact model that is robust, flexible and transparent; and that is able to simulate flood impacts at a global scale.
the results are a useful first approximation of global flood risk.
the model is useful and robust, with the caveat that it is sensitive to flood protection standards and climate forcing datasets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model is a useful, validated tool for estimating global-scale flood risk.
the model is a powerful tool to estimate flood risk at the macro-scale.
the global-scale flood risk assessment presented in this paper is a significant advance on previous studies.

it is now possible to assess flood risk on a global scale.

, although there are still significant uncertainties, we now have a tool that can produce global flood risk maps for a wide range of indicators, and that can be improved as new data becomes available.
